sourceInformation.source: The Wire (2002-2008), kept gritty and real: an original spiritual successor, original characters and a fictional East Side district
sourceInformation.genre: Investigative stealth-adventure with mini-games (surveillance, informant, wiretap, foot chase, interrogation)
sourceInformation.perspective: Three-quarter top-down (engine native), switchable to isometric and top-down with V / R3
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge v0.85.1 handoff engine (one file, no dependencies, patched only to add stick-axis inversion), plain JavaScript, AI Hub session client 1.3.0 (parallel mode); bundled to a single html file
sourceInformation.artDirection: Engine-native HD puppet characters in pixel-art 3/4 view, procedural brick rowhouses and low-rises, rain, night lighting and lamp pools, HTML HUD in a muted gold-on-charcoal theme
sourceInformation.animation: Engine-native procedural Humanoid rigs (IK gait, poses, expressions, E.MOVES tackle) and tweened HUD; no sprite sheets or imported clips
sourceInformation.audio: All synthesized in code: five chip-synth songs (title, stealth, chase, box, report), sound effects, and Animalese-style gibberish voices with a different pitch and wave per speaker; no files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1, parallel mode, 1-4 players, each plays their own copy and reports a case score; passes the hub harness. Outside a hub it is single player
sourceInformation.testing: Headless engine tests (63 system checks plus a 23-check full playthrough) run with exact fixed steps; Playwright browser runs for visuals, mouse, attract mode and a real-time demo; AI Hub harness; WebKit viewport matrix. No real gamepad or real iOS Safari was available: controllers were mocked
sourceInformation.research: Read the engine API card and AI Hub protocol only. The show is known from knowledge; no web research
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux; browser unknown (Chromium and WebKit via Playwright used for testing)
sourceInformation.usage: unknown (cost and token counts are not exposed to the session); session time about 30 minutes

testingFeedback: About 12 real issues: dropped arrest script, key sharing between confirm and interact/tackle, same-frame interact retrigger, overlay left open, attract pilot stalling behind a screen, blocked alley, stale screen on restart, invalid color, missing glyph, overflowing panel, photo line-of-sight ignoring crouch, unreachable photo range.
Four were game breaking: the dropped arrest script (case stuck mid-chase), the attract pilot stalling at the interview, the van restarting forever, and the fully blocked chase alley.
The headless full playthrough with real input actions: it found most logic bugs in seconds, and doubled as the proof that every stage connects.
The mobile viewport matrix: the game is controller/keyboard only, so phone layouts say little beyond the layout being sane.
engineFeedback: Characters that animate and look finished from rigs alone, and the Shell HUD/menus/settings/rebinding that come free.
Slightly: assumed Dialog and key-bound actions were independent (confirm and interact share Space), and that a TileMap legend accepts every character.
Stick-axis inversion in settings (patched into the input poll), the attract-mode pilot, and the interview/wire/listening mini-games.
Knowing what is exposed on game.input and Settings (undocumented fields like padMove, _specs) without reading source.
The standard menu being fixed: I wanted my own settings group names and glyph options and had to edit spec objects.
Make custom settings first-class with apply hooks that cover gamepad axes, so inversion needs no patch.
promptFeedback: Clear, structured requirements: a checklist that is directly testable (attract mode, glyphs, inversion, touch message, hub).
The Source Information block and exit-interview schema are asked for twice in different forms, and Testing/Engine/Prompt questions sit separately from the final reply rules.
Making one coherent, fun game of a TV drama in a single sitting, with 10-foot UI, hub rules and polish all at once.
A real gamepad run, with a DualSense, to confirm the stick-inversion issue and PlayStation glyphs on hardware.

aiHub.name: Wire Tap Dance
aiHub.tagline: Nobody gets convicted by a feeling
aiHub.description: A gritty detective game inspired by The Wire: photograph a drug crew from cover, pay an informant, tap a payphone, run down a runner and break him in the box. Build a case a prosecutor can carry.
aiHub.controls: Stick or WASD move, R2 or Shift sprint, Circle or C crouch, L2 or Q camera, Cross or E interact, Square or J tackle, Triangle or Tab case file, R3 or V change view
